title: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary and Understand the Average Salary in Australia
description: Learn how to convert hourly pay to annual salary using the standard 38-hour week. Includes tax, Medicare, super, and how it compares to the average salary in Australia.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, your annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 1,976 hours (38 × 52).

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, annual gross pay is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly figure accordingly.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor set by the Fair Work Commission, currently $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026). Award rates are higher minimums for specific industries or occupations, set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. Many employees are covered by an award that pays above the national minimum. Casual employees also receive a 25% loading on top of their base rate, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour.

faqs.q: How is tax and Medicare calculated on my annual salary?
faqs.a: The Australian Taxation Office applies a progressive tax scale. For 2026–27, the first $18,200 is tax-free, then 15% up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income, though low-income earners may receive a reduction. These are deducted from your gross annual pay to estimate your take-home amount. Superannuation (12%) is paid on top by your employer, not deducted from your salary.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

If you earn an hourly wage or have been offered a salary, understanding your annual pay is straightforward. The basic formula is **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. This article assumes a standard full-time week of 38 hours unless stated otherwise. For part-time or irregular hours, simply replace 38 with your usual weekly hours.

For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (set by the Fair Work Commission from 1 July 2026), your annual gross pay would be:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44

This figure is before tax, the Medicare levy, and any other deductions. It also does not include superannuation, which your employer pays on top.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly pay by two. Using the minimum wage example:

Weekly: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72
Fortnightly: $1,004.72 × 2 = $2,009.44

You can use [the timesheet](/) to calculate your own figures by entering your base hourly rate and selecting casual loading if applicable.

## Understanding the Average Salary in Australia

The **average salary in Australia** is often quoted from the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings series. As of May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2,083.70 per week, which equates to about $108,352 annually (based on 52 weeks). However, this is an average across all full-time employees, not a median for any specific job. The all-employees total earnings figure (including part-time workers) is $1,579.20 per week, or roughly $82,118 per year.

These averages are useful benchmarks, but your own pay depends on your industry, award, and experience. For more detail, see our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page.

## National Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

It is important to distinguish between different pay rates:

- **National Minimum Wage**: The legal minimum for all employees not covered by an award or agreement. From 1 July 2026 it is $26.44 per hour.
- **Award rates**: Higher minimums set for specific industries or roles by the Fair Work Ombudsman. Most employees are covered by an award.
- **Casual loading**: A 25% addition to the base rate for casual employees, compensating for lack of paid leave. The minimum casual rate is $33.05 per hour.

When using our calculator, enter your **base hourly rate** before any casual loading. Then check the casual loading box to add 25% on top. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

For more on this, visit [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) and [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage).

## Tax and the Medicare Levy on Your Annual Salary

Once you have your annual gross figure, the next step is estimating tax and the Medicare levy. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) uses a progressive tax scale for residents in 2026–27:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001 and above: $51,370 plus 45% of excess over $190,000

In addition, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. Low-income earners may qualify for a reduction (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this estimate).

### Example Tax Calculation

Take the minimum wage annual gross of $52,245.44:

- Tax-free threshold: $18,200
- Taxable amount: $52,245.44 – $18,200 = $34,045.44
- Tax at 15%: $34,045.44 × 0.15 = $5,106.82
- Plus Medicare levy (2% of $52,245.44): $1,044.91
- Total tax and Medicare: $6,151.73
- Estimated take-home pay: $52,245.44 – $6,151.73 = $46,093.71

This is an estimate only. It does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. See our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for more details.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. It does not reduce your gross pay. For the minimum wage example, your employer would contribute an additional $6,269.45 per year (12% of $52,245.44), up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not included in your annual salary figure but is an important part of your total remuneration. Learn more at [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Important Disclaimer

This article provides estimates only. Annual pay is calculated as hourly rate × hours per week × 52, assuming the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. For a personalised calculation, use [the timesheet](/) and refer to official sources such as the Fair Work Ombudsman, Australian Taxation Office, and Australian Bureau of Statistics.
